short: A prominent city-state in ancient Greece, uniquely focused on military training, discipline, and land warfare.
full:
Situated in the Eurotas valley in Laconia, Sparta rose to dominance in the Peloponnese by subjugating its neighbours, whose populations were reduced to state serfs known as helots. To maintain control over this vast enslaved population, Spartan male citizens underwent a rigorous, state-sponsored military education system called the agoge, creating the most formidable land army in classical Greece.

Sparta led the Greek forces to victory during the Greco-Persian Wars and defeated its great rival Athens in the Peloponnesian War. However, continuous warfare, a dwindling citizen population, and decisive defeats by Thebes in the 4th century BCE permanently broke Spartan hegemony.
